content.what_it_is: Third-party MATLAB utility function (Pekka Kumpulainen, Tampere University of Technology, dated 21.5.2012 in the header comment L25-26) bundled in the single_vessel_short_channel postprocessing folder; called by plot_vessel_morpho.m. Creates a grid of Nh x Nw subplot-like axes with user-controlled gaps and margins in normalized figure units. Missing arguments get defaults (gap=.02 L29, marg_h=.05 L30, marg_w=.05 L31); scalar gap/marg_w/marg_h are expanded to 2-element pairs (L33-41). Axis height axh and width axw are computed by dividing the unit square minus margins and inter-axis gaps by the counts (L43-44). Starting from the top row (py = 1-marg_h(2)-axh, L46), a double loop over rows ih=1:Nh and columns ix=1:Nw (L50-62) creates each axes with 'Units','normalized' and 'Position',[px py axw axh] with blanked X/Y tick labels (L55-58), advancing px by axw+gap(2) per column (L59) and dropping py by axh+gap(1) per row (L61). If a second output is requested, pos gets the axes 'Position' properties (L63-65); ha is returned as a column vector (L66).
entities: tight_subplot — function, signature [ha, pos] = tight_subplot(Nh, Nw, gap, marg_h, marg_w), L1
Nh — input, number of axes vertically, L1 (doc L7)
Nw — input, number of axes horizontally, L1 (doc L8)
gap — input, inter-axes gap(s), scalar or [gap_h gap_w], L1 (doc L9-10)
marg_h — input, height margins, scalar or [lower upper], L1 (doc L11-12)
marg_w — input, width margins, scalar or [left right], L1 (doc L13-14)
ha — output, axes handle array (row-wise from upper left), L1 (doc L16-18), built L55, columnized L66
pos — output, axes positions, L1 (doc L19), set L64
py — running normalized y position of current row, L46
px — running normalized x position, L51

equations.ref: axis height from unit figure minus margins and row gaps
axis width from unit figure minus margins and column gaps

unresolved: ha grows without preallocation (assignment at L55; the preallocation ha = zeros(Nh*Nw,1) at L48 is commented out) — handle-class compatibility of numeric preallocation may be why
nargin<4 uses || isempty(marg_h) (L30) but nargin<3 and nargin<5 (L29, L31) do not have the isempty guard — passing [] for gap or marg_w is not defaulted, asymmetry unexplained in this file
